fact: 2010-04-02：Clare 与 Beck 在俄国餐厅约会吃饭（抬头写 Clare 38、Beck 34、Alba 36）；Clare 为穿什么纠结到迟到，最后选了黑裙 + 极少的首饰；Beck 比她更晚，为开久的会道歉；两人都穿黑裙。
quote: Friday, April 2, 2010 (Clare is 38, Beck is 34, Alba is 36) … Clare: I am nervous about meeting Rebecka again, and I spend so much time dithering about what to wear that I end up being late. … I finally opted for safety with a black dress and minimal jewelry.

fact: Clare 说「我习惯等」，因为 Henry「time-challenged」；Beck 说自己的丈夫总迟到、让她发疯；点菜：Beck 吃素，要罗宋汤和南瓜馅饼，Clare 要罗宋汤和土豆饼；上酒时侍者讲规矩——先闻黑面包、抿一口伏特加、吃腌黄瓜、咬一口面包，如此重复。
quote: “I’m used to waiting. My husband was very, um, time-challenged.” … “I’m a vegetarian, so it’s nice to see all the meat-free items. I’m a big fan of beets, I’ve got to try the borscht.” … He explains the ritual: Inhale the smell of the bread, sip the vodka, eat the pickles, take a bite of bread, repeat.

fact: Clare 环视餐厅，发现 Beck 是店里唯一的黑人；她提到怀孕时常来吃浓汤和罗宋汤；Alba 八岁，Henry 死时 Alba 五岁（她脑海里闪过血与 Alba 的脸）。
quote: Beck glances around, and I realize that she’s the only Black person in the restaurant. … “Alba is eight.” … “. . . Henry died? She was five.” The scene flashes in my mind: the blood, Alba’s face . . .

fact: Beck 讲 Jasper：MIT 研究生院相识，他「mercurial」，把她迷得神魂颠倒，认识六个月就结婚（「Big mistake」）；他们有个女儿，出生时死了；两人没走出来，靠工作撑住；MacArthur 奖是两人共同的，现在仍远程合作但不知还能多久；Jasper 近来极不稳定，「unsettling when you realize you can't trust the person you used to trust most in the world」。
quote: “Jasper and I met in grad school, at MIT. He’s very—mercurial. … We got married six months after we met. Big mistake” … “We had a daughter. She died at birth.” … “The MacArthur Award was to both of us, together” … “He’s been incredibly erratic lately.”

fact: 一个裸体女人从旋转门里跌进来，湿、脏、长发打结夹灰，看着近四十岁——是 Alba；Clare 把自己的大衣披上、围巾绕上、给她面包、二十美元钞票，最后连鞋也脱给她；Alba 说「I was having a hard time」，又惊觉「2010? Oh, shit.」，改口坐出租车回家、答应把大衣送回。
quote: there’s a naked person in the revolving door of the restaurant. … Of course it’s Alba. Oh, god, she looks awful. … She might be in her late thirties. … “2010? Oh, shit. Jeez, of course, I’m sorry, I should have realized! I’d better go.”

fact: Alba 走后，Beck 低声说「Charisse told me」；Clare 承认那是她女儿；Beck 说她像 Clare，Clare 说她更像 Henry——「尤其刚才她差不多到他那个年纪」；Clare 把这当成好兆头：「如果成年后的 Alba 见到你不惊讶，那说明我们做朋友这事有戏」。
quote: Beck leans toward me and murmurs, “Charisse told me.” … “She looks like you.” … “Of you and me becoming friends. If my grown-up Alba is unsurprised to see you, it bodes well.”

fact: 两人聊出身与信仰：Clare 在密歇根 South Haven 的富裕家庭长大、SAIC；Beck 是底特律学者家庭的女儿、Cranbrook 再 MIT；两人政治上都偏激进；Clare 天主教（母亲死后全家不去教堂，「像断了电」），Beck 贵格会（家族自地下铁道时代起就是贵格派，母亲家有白人，父母在聚会所相识）。
quote: growing up in Michigan (me, in a wealthy family in tiny lakeside South Haven, Beck as the daughter of academics in Detroit); art school (me, SAIC, her, Cranbrook and then MIT) … “The Quakers were strong abolitionists, and both sides of my family have been various sorts of Quakers going back to Underground Railroad times.”

fact: Beck 问时间旅行让她更信还是更不信神，Clare 答「更不信」：宇宙随机无意义；她解释规则——知道的事无法改变（9/11 时朋友怪 Henry 没阻止），「As long as we don’t know, we’re free」；Beck 说出「A block universe」，Clare 说正是；提到芝加哥大学 David Kendrick 的论文、他为军方做研究、病人被人肉、政客不想让公众相信；Alba 班上所有孩子都知道这事。
quote: “Less,” I say without hesitation. “It makes the universe seem random and pointless.” … “Time travelers can’t change anything. After 9/11 a few of our friends were angry with Henry because he didn’t prevent it from happening.” … “A block universe,” Beck says.

fact: Clare 低声讲 2016 年总统大选，Beck 举手制止：「No. That’s horrible.」「How do we stop—」，Clare 说「We don’t… We can’t.」，Beck 说「We have to!」声音发抖；Clare 改用「时空是一所无数房间的大房子」的比喻解释；Beck 要她说点好消息，Clare 说「基因治疗会成功，他们明年宣布」。
quote: “No. That’s horrible,” she says. She looks ill. “How do we stop—” … “We don’t,” I say gently. “We can’t.” … “Tell me something good, to counterbalance all that bad you just laid on me.” “Gene therapy works. They announce it next year.”

fact: 碰杯：Beck 说「To life, out of order」，Clare 回「To world enough, and time」——那是 Henry 最喜欢的祝酒词；Beck 邀她去工作室看那座博物馆、体验虚拟现实；出租车司机把大衣和鞋送回（「The lady took care of it」），Beck 已付账、说「下次你付」；两人在雨棚下拥抱告别，Clare 走在冰雨里想「这就是选择一个人的感觉：没有一件事是确定的，一切都有可能」，觉得自己的未来开了花。
quote: “To life, out of order,” she says. “‘To world enough, and time,’” I reply. It was Henry’s favorite toast, but it seems appropriate tonight. … “You can get it next time,” she says when I protest. … I realize that this is what it’s like to choose someone; nothing is certain, everything is possible. I feel my future blossom.
